output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show that from 4 Oct 22:10, every Veltranol job received a 36-month shelf life from PackBridge, and no operator overrode it. Jobs before that, including those after the firmware change and those set up by agency operators, were correct at 24 months. The ERP trail shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, valid only from 1 Mar 2027. The value in effect is still 24. So the trigger was that master-data edit. Somewhere between the ERP and PackBridge, the future-dated value was used early. This contradicts the vendor's statement that this cannot happen. I have not found how that happens. Two Line 1 day-shift lots are also affected and sit in the warehouse, so the problem is not confined to Line 3 nights. Do not warn or remove the agency operators. Do not switch off the camera, which only checks the print against the job. Instead, hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record, and correct the ERP record. Also inspect the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Ask Corvane and IT to explain why a future-dated value was read. I am fairly confident in this. Whether other products are affected is unconfirmed.
